findings.explanation: On lsServer, `assocState` takes associated, associating, disassociating, failed or unassociated. `configState` takes applied, applying, failed-to-apply or not-applied. `pending-reboot` is a value of `operState`. `establishing` and `unsupported-config` are not valid for these fields.
findings.quote: the association to a physical node (`associated`, `unassociated`, `establishing`, and failure classes such as `failed`) and the push state of the policy bundle (`applied`, `not-applied`, `pending-reboot`, `failed-to-apply`, `applying`, `unsupported-config`)
findings.suggested_fix: Correct the enum lists. Explain that pending-reboot and pending-reassociation come from `operState`, and include `operState` in the data-source field list.

findings.explanation: The Splunk Add-on for Cisco UCS gives all data the single sourcetype `cisco:ucs`, with `source=cisco:ucs:<classId>` (here `cisco:ucs:lsServer`). It ships neither `cisco:ucs:inventory` nor `cisco:ucs:audit`.
findings.suggested_fix: Describe the feed as `sourcetype=cisco:ucs source=cisco:ucs:lsServer`, or document a deliberate local sourcetype override on the input. Update the Step 1 probes to match.

findings.explanation: The Splunkbase catalog and the add-on docs both give the app id as `Splunk_TA_cisco-ucs`, with a hyphen.
findings.quote: The on-disk and canonical add-on id uses an underscore; older download bundles may still show a hyphen in the filename.

findings.explanation: With the current SPL, the PendingReboot bucket can never be populated, because it tests `configState` for an `operState` value.
findings.quote: Timechart of daily `Drifted` and `PendingReboot` rows during a template roll-out
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the panel only after the PendingReboot logic is based on `operState`.

findings.explanation: The sourcetype and several enum values do not match the product, so the UC cannot have been validated against live data.
findings.suggested_fix: Downgrade status until the search has been checked against a real lsServer feed.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: The `compliance` case tests `confg="pending-reboot"` and `confg="unsupported-config"`, which are not configState values. It also tests `assoc="establishing"/"throttled"/"removing"`, which are not assocState values. PendingReboot can never fire, and real `associating`/`disassociating` profiles fall into Unknown. Use `operState` for pending-reboot.
`sourcetype="cisco:ucs:inventory"` is not emitted by the add-on; all events are `sourcetype=cisco:ucs`, with the class in `source`.

`stats ... by org, name, dn, compliance` gives one row per state seen in 24 hours. A profile that was Drifted earlier and is Compliant now still produces a Drifted row, and the alert fires on it. Take the latest state per `dn` first (for example `stats latest(compliance) ... by dn`).
The `org` regex `^org-root/(.+)/ls-[^/]+$` does not match profiles directly under root (`org-root/ls-X`), so `org` ends up as the full dn for those profiles.

summary: A clearly written service-profile posture UC whose state vocabulary is partly invented. `pending-reboot` is an `operState` value, not a `configState` value, and `establishing`, `throttled`, `removing` and `unsupported-config` are not lsServer enums. It also relies on a `cisco:ucs:inventory` sourcetype and an underscore app directory that the add-on does not ship.
